text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- CPMF WILL REDUCE BANK LIQUIDITY
An upcoming special tax on financial transactions known as the CPMF will reduce liquidity in the banking system, which would cut the availability of credit and slow the economy a bit.
--BAMERINDUS SOLUTION COULD BE DELAYED TWO MONTHS
A solution for troubled private bank Bamerindus, which is under Central Bank intervention, might not come for another two months, according to a Central Bank official.
--EUROPE OPPOSES BRAZIL AUTO-IMPORT POLICY

The European Union's ambassador in Brazil said the union would seek formal consultations with Brazil before the World Trade Organization to discuss Brazil's auto-import rules. The United States requested consultations over the issue last week.
O GLOBO
-- BANKERS TO TESTIFY AT INQUIRY INTO ILLEGAL DEBT ISSUES
A senator leading an investigation into the illegal issuance of state and municipal debt will ask bank directors to testify.
--CARDOSO PERSONALLY TAKES CHARGE OF RE-ELECTION ISSUE
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso will personally take charge this week of the controversial re-election debate, hoping to force a full vote on the issue in the lower house on Jan 29.
--CENTRAL BANK'S FRANCO SAYS '97 RESERVES TO HIT $70 BLN
Central Bank International Affairs Director Gustavo Franco said Brazil's international reserves would grow to $70 billion in 1997, compared to about $60 billion at the end of 1996.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- GOVERNMENT OWES ONE BILLION REAIS TO LAND OWNERS
Brasilia's land reform agency Incra owes some 1.063 billion reais to land owners who had property confiscated by the government but never received reimbursment.
-- SAO PAULO SAW FEWER MURDERS IN 1996
Some 4,826 people were murdered in the city of Sao Paulo in 1996, compared to 4,990 the year before.
* Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--John Miller, Sao Paulo newsroom, 5511 248-5414
